question.text: Which of the following is the graph of $y=\ln {(x-4)} ?$
question.explanation:
To plot $y=\ln {(x-4)},$ we apply the following steps:

  • Take the curve $y=\ln {x}.$
  • Translate it by $4$ units to the right to get the graph of $y=\ln {(x-4)}.$

question.text: The point $A$ with coordinates $(2,\ln2)$ lies on the curve $y=\ln{x},$ and the point $A'$ with coordinates $(6,\ln2)$ lies on the curve $y=\ln(ax),$ shown above. What is the value of $a?$
question.explanation:
The graph of $y=\ln(ax)$ can be obtained from $y=\ln x$ by a horizontal stretch of scale factor $\dfrac{1}{a}.$

From the diagram, we deduce that under such a transformation, the point $(2,\ln2)$ that lies on $y=\ln x$ becomes

\[ \left(\dfrac{1}{a} \cdot 2,\ln 2 \right)=\left(6, \ln 2\right) \]

which lies on $y=\ln (ax).$

Therefore, $a=\dfrac 13.$

question.text: The point $A$ with coordinates $(4,\ln 4)$ lies on the curve $y=\ln{x},$ and the point $A'$ with coordinates $\left(1,\ln4\right)$ lies on the curve $y=\ln(ax),$ shown above. What is the value of $a?$
question.explanation:
The graph of $y=\ln(ax)$ can be obtained from $y=\ln x$ by a horizontal stretch of scale factor $\dfrac{1}{a}.$

From the diagram, we deduce that under such a transformation, the point $(4,\ln4)$ that lies on $y=\ln x$ becomes

\[ \left(\dfrac{1}{a} \cdot 4,\ln 4 \right)=\left(1, \ln 4\right) \]

which lies on $y=\ln (ax).$

Therefore, $a=4.$

question.text: Which of the following is the graph of $y=4\log_3(x-2)-1?$
question.explanation:
To plot $y=4\log_3 (x-2)-1,$ we apply the following steps:

  • Take the curve $y=\log_3 x.$

  • Translate it by $2$ unit to the right to get the graph of $y=\log_3 (x-2).$

  • Then, stretch the result by a scale factor of $4$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=4\log_3 (x-2).$
  • Finally, translate the result by $1$ unit down to get the graph of $y=4\log_3 (x-2)-1.$

  • Then, stretch the result by a scale factor of $2$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=2\ln(x+3).$

exampleAnswers.title: Finding Unknown Parameters Given a Transformed Logarithmic Function

question.text: The diagram above shows the graph of $y=k\log_2 (bx).$ Find the value of $k\cdot b.$
question.explanation:
Clearly, $b\neq 0.$ Substituting $x=\dfrac1b$ into the equation of the curve, we get

\begin{align} y &= k\log_2 \left(b\cdot\dfrac1b\right) \\[5pt] &= k\log_2 1 \\[5pt] &= 0. \end{align}

So, the point $\left(\dfrac1b, 0\right)$ lies on the curve. But from the diagram, we know that $(3,0)$ lies on the curve. Hence

\[ (3,0) = \left(\dfrac1b,0\right)\quad\Rightarrow\quad b=\dfrac13. \]

Now, we substitute coordinates of the point $(6,2)$ into the equation:

\begin{align} k\log_2 (bx) &= y \\[5pt] k\log_2 \left(\dfrac13x\right) &= y \\[5pt] k\log_2 \left(\dfrac13\cdot 6\right) &= 2 \\[5pt] k\log_2 2 &= 2 \\[5pt] k &= 2 \end{align}

Finally,

\[ k\cdot b = 2 \cdot \dfrac13 = \dfrac23. \]

question.text: The diagram above shows the graph of $y=\log_4 (x-d)+c.$ Find the value of $\dfrac{d}{c}.$
question.explanation:
In the given graph, the vertical asymptote is $x=4.$ So, the argument of the logarithm function should evaluate to zero at $x=4.$ Therefore,

\[ 4-d = 0\quad\Rightarrow\quad d=4. \]

Now, we substitute coordinates of the point $\left(8,3\right)$ into the equation:

\begin{align*} \log_4 (x-d)+c &= y \\[3pt] \log_4 (x-4)+c &= y \\[3pt] \log_4 (8-4)+c &= 3 \\[3pt] \log_4 (4)+c &= 3 \\[3pt] 1+c &= 3 \\[3pt] c &=2 \end{align*}

Finally,

\[ \dfrac{d}{c} = \dfrac42 = 2. \]
